newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - Swedish unemployment seen 8.4 pct Feb.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Swedish unemployment seen 8.4 pct Feb.

text.p: Swedish unemployment was expected to fall to 8.4 percent in February, according to a Reuters poll of 14 analysts on Tuesday.
Forecasts varied between 8.2 percent and 8.7 percent.
In January Swedish open unemployment was 8.8 percent and in February last year 7.7 percent.
Open unemployment does not include people on government training scheme or in government sponsored jobs.
For calendar 1997 analysts forecast an average rate of 7.8 percent with forecasts ranging between 7.3 percent and 8.6 percent.
In 1996 Sweden's unemployment rate was on average 8.1 percent.

Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Carnegie, Chase, Consensus, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, HSBC Midland Bank, IDEA, J P Morgan, Lehman Brothers, Merrill Lynch, Nordbanken, S-E-Banken, and Swedbank.
Monthly figures only were available from Chase, Consensus, HSBC Midland Bank, J P Morgan, Merrill Lynch, and S-E-Banken.
Stastistics Sweden will publish Feburary unemployment data on March 7 at 1200 GMT.
